Verse 1
The kettle sighs before I do,
steam drawing ghosts along the pane.
I count the streetlights, two by two,
a habit strange as static rain.
My shadow's grown a little bored
of pacing rooms it knows too well.
The clock ticks slow, a metronome
for something I can never tell.

Chorus
I am an island, calm and small,
a lighthouse dimmed but never dark.
I send my signal to the wall
and wait to see it leave a mark.
Quiet isn't quite the same
as empty, though they wear one name.
I'm learning how to hold this space
without a second in the frame.

Verse 2
The aquarium hums three doors down,
blue light spilling on the floor.
I water plants that make no sound,
and greet the mirror like before.
Some evenings I rehearse a joke
for no one waiting on the line.
The dial tone is a kind of smoke
that curls and settles, thin and fine.

Chorus
I am an island, calm and small,
a lighthouse dimmed but never dark.
I send my signal to the wall
and wait to see it leave a mark.
Quiet isn't quite the same
as empty, though they wear one name.
I'm learning how to hold this space
without a second in the frame.

Bridge
Somewhere a moth taps glass for light,
mistaking distance for a door.
I understand that appetite,
that reaching toward an empty shore.
But I have learned to name the hush,
to let it settle, let it be —
a tide that doesn't need to rush
to prove its calm belongs to me.

Final Chorus
I am an island, calm and whole,
a lighthouse steady, softly bright.
I send my signal, let it roll
across the static of the night.
Quiet isn't quite the same
as empty, though they wear one name.
I've learned to furnish this small space
and call it, gently, home.

[Verse 1]

the coffee boiled over and I didn't care,
your sweater's still hanging on the back of my chair.
There's a hum in my ribs like a tuning fork,
every ordinary minute starts to talk,
and the mundane goes shimmering, gold at the seams,
since you wandered into my geometry of dreams.

[Pre-Chorus]
My thoughts arrive in bright disorder now,
a flock of sparrows scattering somehow,
and every plan I had gets rearranged,
the moment that you smiled, the weather changed.

[Chorus]

a marigold burst in a gray afternoon,
I'm cartwheeling drunk on this feeling within,
happy and reckless and tethered to you.
Call it combustion, call it delight,
call it the voltage that hums through the night,
I'll take the tumble, I'll take the fall,
you're the best kind of trouble I've had at all.

you laugh at your own jokes before they are born,
I catalog freckles the way sailors chart stars,
I'm rearranging my orbit around who you are.

we're building a nonsense we're happy to find,
a language of glances, a Morse code of grins,
and every door I walk through, our story begins.

Verse 1

Verse 1

Verse 3

carrying what's left of your name.
